about.purpose: Selector map that re-scopes the React Button's OWN compiled CSS onto the legacy classic-admin button classes, so classic wp-admin renders identically to the React component. This is the single source of the generation step (generate.mjs).
about.source: packages/components/build-style/style.css — every rule whose selector starts with `.components-button` is extracted and its selector rewritten via the map below. Declarations are taken verbatim (already token-based), so classic gets React's exact implementation, including the transparent-border + outline/outline-offset focus construction.
about.contract: Legacy selectors and markup (.button, .button-primary, .wp-core-ui, get_submit_button() output) are preserved; only React's declarations are re-pointed onto them.

height.why: 40px is always the default button size (Joen's ruling). React's base height is 36px with 40px behind `.is-next-40px-default-size`; classic has no such class, so we fold 40px into the base and drop the opt-in rule. Excludes small (24px) and compact (32px) so those keep their own heights, and excludes link (auto height).

dropped.note: React selectors with no classic equivalent are dropped; where dropped, classic keeps Core's own buttons.css rule for that case (our stylesheet overrides only what it emits).

selectors.reason: Classic uses `.button-link-delete`; kept from Core's buttons.css.
React-only busy animation class; classic markup has no `.is-busy`.
React icon-slot layout; classic `<input type=submit>` cannot host icon children. Icon buttons handled separately.
React uses `.dashicon`; classic uses `.dashicons` (plural). Different class; left to Core.
